the Palomar transient factory survey has detected a highly subluminous type II-P supernova, PTF10vdi, that has a very low peak luminosity and is one of the most rapidly declining type II-P supernovae known.
we have discovered and characterized a new class of low luminosity Type II-P supernova, and that the PTF is the first optical survey with the ability to detect supernovae within hours of explosion.

the study of the most energetic transient sources of the Universe.

the PTF is now a fully integrated and operational system, and is capable of detecting and characterizing a wide variety of transient phenomena in real-time.

we have demonstrated that the PTF can provide the real-time detection of a wide variety of optical transient events and the rapid-response follow-up of these events in the optical and other wavelength bands.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PTF is capable of detecting and characterizing optical transients at a level that rivals or exceeds that of the most sensitive radio and X-ray facilities, and that the PTF's unique combination of real-time discovery and multiwavelength follow up is a powerful tool for understanding the physics and evolution of a wide range of transient phenomena.

the combination of a large field of view with high-cadence imaging is a powerful tool to detect and study rare and exotic transients, and to provide a new window on the physics of more common transients.
